about: Generated by tools/intuicode_index.mjs from the data the writers export. Do not edit by hand: run node tools/intuicode_index.mjs.

folders.name: Settings
folders.about: Settings holds starting values the whole program shares: limits, names, lists of options. Only set values here. Nothing is shown or asked.

folders.name: Tools
folders.about: Tools holds reusable actions. Each tool starts with "define" and does its work in the indented lines under it. Tools only run when Main program runs them.

folders.name: Main program
folders.about: Main program is what actually happens when you press Run, step by step from the top.

sentences.tip: Creates a name or changes what it holds. Names can have spaces: "high score" becomes high_score.

Leave off "by …" to go down by 1.

Show several things on one line by joining them with "and".
Anything in {curly brackets} inside text is replaced by its current value.
The answer is always text.

examples.title: Get a number from someone
examples.say: ask for a number "How old are you? " and store in age

examples.title: Keep going until something happens
examples.say:
repeat forever
    ask "Password? " and store in guess
    if guess is "open sesame"
        stop the loop

examples.title: Make a reusable tool
examples.say:
define double using n
    give back n times 2

examples.title: Write it naturally
examples.say:
please ask for a number "Age? " and store in age then show age
if age is at least 18 then show "Welcome"
note: "please", "just" and "then" are fine. Filler is left out, and "then" splits steps.

examples.title: Use a tool and keep its answer
examples.say: run double with 21 and store in answer

examples.title: Keep a list of things
examples.say:
create list basket with "apples", "bread"
add "milk" to basket
for each item in basket
    show "-" and item

folders.name: Structure
folders.about: Structure is what is on the page, top to bottom. Indent a line to put it inside the section, list or form above it.

sentences.tip: Shown in the browser tab.
One per page: the main title.
The name is how Styling and Mechanics refer to it.

sentences.say: add a text box called ‹name› with hint "‹hint›"
sentences.tip: Also: number box, password box, email box, big text box.

sentences.say: add a number box called ‹name› allowing decimals, from ‹0› to ‹100›
sentences.tip: Also: in steps of 5, at least 1, at most 10, with a number keypad. A time box picks a time.
Mechanics: "if ‹name› is ticked", "tick ‹name›", "untick ‹name›".

sentences.say: add a slider called ‹name› from ‹0› to ‹100›
sentences.tip: Its value is where it is set, as text.

Indent "add a list item "…"" under it.
Add to the end of any line to put it in a group (a CSS class).

folders.name: Styling
folders.about: Styling is how things look. Style an element by its name, a group, or every element of a kind.

sentences.tip: Separate styles with commas.
A group is a CSS class. Reuse it on many elements.
Adds the group to an element in Structure.
Indent styles under it for phones.
Then use "background the colour main".
A piece added at the start of the element, by CSS alone. "after ‹name›:" adds one at the end. content: attr(data-‹x›) shows a value Mechanics stored on the element.

folders.name: Mechanics
folders.about: Mechanics is what the page does. Most of it starts with "when … is clicked" or "when the page has loaded".

sentences.tip: Indent what should happen.
The page won't reload.
The time can be a name too: "every gap seconds".
Named, so "stop ‹ticker›" can stop it (clearInterval). Also "after 3 seconds as ‹reminder›".
Indent the lines that might fail; then "if it fails" at the same indent, with what to do instead.
"if it fails as problem" keeps the error: problem.message says what went wrong. "in any case" runs either way.
Waits for something that finishes later. Add "and store in ‹name›" to keep what it gives back.
About 60 times a second: move things, then draw them.
Once, near the top of Mechanics. Then "if "left" is held".
left, right, up, down, space, or a letter.
Once per press. For holding a key down, use "is held" inside "every frame".
A finger or a mouse. "tap x" and "tap y" say where.
A finger lifting or a mouse button let go over it. Also "when the screen is released", anywhere.
Again and again as it moves; "tap x" and "tap y" say where it is now.
Wipes a drawing area, ready for the next frame.
